payload.headline: SPY closes on its 200-day line; QQQ stays below its 681.80 gate

summary.thesis: Tech (QQQ) is in a downtrend and the broad market (SPY) is sideways. SPY closed at 730.2, right on its 200-day average of 730.02. Only 15% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, and fear was elevated at 25.46 on Nov 17.
summary.decision: Stand aside on new buying for both long-term and swing positions.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 681.80 (its 200-day average) ends the tech downtrend under the market gate. A SPY close below 730.02 would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.

payload.happening: On Nov 18, SPY closed at 730.2, down 0.31% on the day. It is down 3.9% over five days and 5.55% over 20 days. That close is below its 1-month low of 732.44 from Nov 17, so SPY is still setting lower closes. It sits 0.0% above its 200-day average of 730.02. QQQ rose 0.39% to 659.51. It is still down 4.47% over five days and 9.06% over 20 days, and it remains below both its 50-day average (714.26) and its 200-day average (681.8). The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. No news has been stored since the last note.
payload.business: Trend, fear and breadth all point the same way. On trend, QQQ is below both of its averages, which means its trend is down. SPY is below its 50-day average but at its 200-day average, so its short trend is broken and its long trend is barely holding. On fear, the VIX was 25.46 on Nov 17, up from 22.91. That is in the 'elevated' band (20 to 30) and ranks in the 94th percentile of the last 252 daily readings, whose range was 13.47 to 31.05. On breadth, only 15% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so the selling is broad and not limited to a few large names. Together these readings describe a market under pressure, with the broad index sitting on its last long-term support line.

worth.text: No valuation is implied. The levels in this note mark price trends only, not what the indices are worth.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: SPY is still 0.0% above its 200-day average of 730.02, so its long-term trend technically holds.
QQQ rose 0.39% on the day and is 1.9% above its 1-month low of 647.05 from Nov 5, so that low is holding for now.
A QQQ close above 681.80 would end the tech downtrend under the market gate.
bear: QQQ is 8.3% below its 50-day average and 3.4% below its 200-day average. Its trend is down.
SPY closed below its 1-month low of 732.44, so the decline is continuing. Losing 730.02 would put its long-term trend down.
Breadth is 15% and fear is elevated at 25.46 (94th percentile of the past 252 readings), which shows broad, nervous selling.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average and the market gate. A close above it ends the tech downtrend, which would support a selective stance.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check, which would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close below it would put the broad market's long-term trend down.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 17). SPY closed 0.3% below it. A close back above it would mean the recent low is holding.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

longterm.why: QQQ remains below its 200-day gate of 681.80. SPY is making lower closes and sits right on its 200-day average of 730.02. Breadth is 15% and fear is elevated. All three readings argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 681.80.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 659.51, 8.3% below its 50-day average of 714.26. Under the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: Two releases are due Nov 25 at 08:30: the second estimate of Q3 GDP and corporate profits, and October Personal Income and Outlays, which includes PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation measure. The latest stored VIX is from Nov 17 because the Nov 18 reading isn't stored yet. SPY's test of 730.02 is the closest level to watch.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 681.80 would end the tech downtrend under the market gate and would support moving to selective. A QQQ close above 714.26 would support leaning in more.

A SPY close below 730.02, or a QQQ close below 647.05, would strengthen the case for standing aside, because the long-term trend in the broad market would be down or the tech decline would be continuing.
payload.what_changed: Since the Nov 17 note, breadth fell from 18% to 15%. The stored VIX moved from the Nov 16 reading to Nov 17's 25.46, up from 22.91. SPY's 1-month low is now 732.44 (Nov 17), replacing 733.00, and SPY closed below it again. The moving averages shifted: QQQ's 200-day is 681.8 (was 681.58), QQQ's 50-day is 714.26 (was 715.38), SPY's 50-day is 762.28 (was 762.89) and SPY's 200-day is 730.02 (was 729.79). QQQ edged up from 656.95 to 659.51. The previous note flagged NVDA earnings after the Nov 17 close, but no news has been stored since then, so this note doesn't cover the result. Both decisions stay at stand aside.
